ES.label: S&P 500 Fut
ES.source: S&P 500 E-mini September contract, +4.25 points, Perplexity consolidated feed stamped 11:10 UTC, priced off Wednesday's 7676.50 settle. Overnight range 7661.25 to 7694.50. Flat is the story. Two sessions ago this board was pricing a synchronised global repricing of the cost of money; Wednesday reversed a large part of it and the overnight tape has held that reversal rather than giving it back. Wednesday's CASH close was 7666.60, up 0.460% from Tuesday's 7631.47 - the first green session in four. NOT ATH: the cash index sits -1.698% below its record close of 7798.99 set 8/13/26 and -1.920% below the 7816.70 record intraday high from the same session. The index has now spent three weeks failing to retake mid-August levels, which is a consolidation, not a downtrend.

NQ.label: Nasdaq 100 Fut
NQ.source: Nasdaq 100 E-mini September contract, -20.50 points, -0.07%, Perplexity consolidated feed stamped 11:10 UTC off Wednesday's 29186.25 settle. Overnight range 29075.00 to 29292.75 - a 218-point swing that resolved almost exactly flat, which is what a market digesting a very large earnings report looks like. Broadcom beat on revenue and on AI semiconductor revenue and still trades about 3% lower pre-market on a gross-margin guide, and the index has absorbed that without breaking. Wednesday's CASH close was 29143.33, up 0.227% from 29077.22. NOT ATH: -4.949% below the 6/2/26 record close of 30660.60 and -5.263% below the 6/3/26 record high of 30762.20. Three months on, the Nasdaq 100 has still not made a new high - the AI trade is being repriced on margin, not on demand.

SOX.label: Philadelphia Semis
SOX.source: Polygon daily bar, Wednesday cash settle, +50.64 points, +0.449%. A green session but the weakest bounce of the four US equity boards, and that ordering matters: semis fell 2.14% Tuesday and recovered less than a quarter of it Wednesday. NOT ATH, and not close - the index is -22.52% below its record close of 14634.72 set 6/22/26. That is the single widest drawdown on this board and it has been widening, not narrowing, for ten weeks. Broadcom's Q4 gross-margin guide of roughly 73% against 78% a year ago is the cleanest available explanation: custom AI accelerators are enormous revenue at structurally lower margin than the merchant silicon they are displacing, and the semiconductor complex is being marked down for mix even as unit demand compounds.

DJI.label: Dow Jones Ind
DJI.source: Polygon daily bar, Wednesday cash settle, +295.07 points, +0.559%. The best of the four boards Wednesday, which is the mirror image of Tuesday when the Dow was the most defensive loser. A cyclical, rate-sensitive, low-duration index leading a bounce that began with a weak ADP print is internally consistent: softer labour data lowers the discount rate before it lowers earnings. NOT ATH: -2.368% below the record close of 54349.12 set 8/5/26. The Russell 2000 gained 1.13% to 2953.17 on the same session, a wider small-cap bounce that says the same thing about rates.

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Cboe VIX, Wednesday settle, down 1.14 points or -6.98% from Tuesday's 16.34. Wednesday's intraday high was 16.82, so the index opened in the panic and closed well outside it - a full round trip. This is the most informative number on the board. Two sessions ago volatility was bid on a global rates shock; it has now given back the entire move and sits inside the 14 to 16 band that has contained it since late July. The Nasdaq analogue VXN settled 21.07, down 4.05% from 21.96, also falling. Note the freshness discipline here: Polygon served a 2026-09-03 pre-open VIX bar at 15.34 and Investing.com's page was showing Wednesday's session as though live. Neither was used. A falling VIX into a payrolls print is the setup that punishes complacency, and Friday is payrolls.

US10Y.label: US 10Y Yield
US10Y.source: US 10-year Treasury yield, 4.785%, down 0.9 basis points from Wednesday's 4.794% close, overnight range 4.755% to 4.787%, page stamped Real-time Data 06:25:19 and verified independently of the 2-year page. Off the 52-week high printed Tuesday. The move is small in isolation and important in context: the entire hawkish impulse that drove this yield to a one-year high has stalled, and it stalled on a labour-market miss rather than on anything the Fed said. Reads as a level, not a percentage - the tile's delta is the percentage change in the yield itself, which is roughly one basis point here, not 0.19% of anything. Treasury announces 3-year, 10-year and 30-year auctions around 11:00 this morning for next week's settlement.

US2Y.label: US 2Y Yield
US2Y.source: US 2-year Treasury yield, 4.379%, down 1.5 basis points from Wednesday's 4.394%, overnight range 4.377% to 4.408%, page stamped Real-time Data 08:08:21 and timestamped separately from the 10-year. The front end is falling faster than the long end, which is the correct signature for a dovish repricing driven by labour data: the 2-year is the Fed-expectations instrument. That puts 2s10s at roughly 40.6 basis points, a modest steepening from Wednesday. Worth stating plainly that the curve is positively sloped and steepening while the market still prices a 61% chance of a HIKE this month - the bond market is pricing one more hike and then a long pause, not a hiking cycle.

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: WTI front-month crude, $92.31, +1.43% from Wednesday's $91.01 settle, overnight range $89.60 to $93.13. Contract month re-verified this run rather than assumed - lesson from the run where WTI front was October while Brent front was November, so the roll is checked independently on each leg every session. Oil is the discordant instrument on the board: every other risk gauge eased overnight while crude firmed more than a percent. The Hormuz picture is genuinely quieter - no new US or Israeli action inside the window and the Wall Street Journal reporting the administration is weighing declaring the war over - yet transit volumes remain badly impaired at six vessels Wednesday against a ten-day average near thirteen. Reduced flow with reduced shooting still means reduced flow.

BRENT.label: Brent Crude
BRENT.source: Brent front-month, $96.63, +1.05% from Wednesday's $95.63, overnight range $94.02 to $97.62. Contract month confirmed separately from WTI. The Brent-WTI spread sits near $4.32, wide enough to keep US export economics attractive and consistent with a supply-side rather than demand-side bid. Brent above $96 with the VIX at 15 is an unusual pair, and it is the pair that should worry an equity investor more than either number alone: the equity market has priced the Gulf risk down to nothing while the physical crude market has not. Iran struck Kuwait early Thursday and the missile was intercepted, which is both an escalation and a demonstration of intact air defence. No verified war-risk insurance datapoint exists inside the window, so none is published here.

GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: Gold futures, $4,476.60, +1.40% from Wednesday's $4,414.60, overnight range $4,426.70 to $4,490.00. This is the third leg of the same trade and the cleanest confirmation that the hawkish scare has broken. Gold fell three consecutive sessions into Tuesday as real yields rose and the dollar firmed; it has now risen two sessions as both reversed. Silver is up 1.12% alongside. The dollar index at 99.09 is down 0.51% overnight and made its low of the session at 99.08, so this is a genuine dollar-debasement bid rather than a pure safe-haven one - equities are flat and credit is quiet, which is not the configuration in which gold rallies for fear reasons.

BTC.label: Bitcoin
BTC.source: Bitcoin, $77,897.96, +0.76%, overnight range $76,993.97 to $78,093.95, fetched from the consolidated crypto feed and cross-checked against the Polygon X:BTCUSD daily series, which puts Wednesday's close at $77,305.10 and Monday's at $78,566.10. Bitcoin fell 0.121% Wednesday while every equity board rose, and it is now recovering that on the softer dollar. The instrument has decoupled from the AI-equity complex over the last fortnight and is trading much more like a dollar-liquidity asset than a risk asset, which makes it a reasonable cross-check on the debasement read that gold is giving. It remains well below its own highs and is not making a directional statement here.

EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: Euro-yen, 181.18, down 1.45% from 183.85, overnight range 181.05 to 184.18, consolidated feed stamped 11:17 UTC. This tile required work: Investing.com's euro-yen page was still displaying Wednesday's session as live, which would have understated the move to roughly flat. It was caught by cross-checking euro-dollar, which is UP 0.16% overnight - a falling euro-yen against a rising euro-dollar can only be yen strength - and confirmed on MarketWatch at 181.42 stamped 6:44 a.m. EDT. The driver is a hawkish Bank of Japan repricing: Bloomberg reports the BoJ favours a 25 basis point hike, board member Takata has discussed larger or consecutive moves, and BoJ accounts confirm there was NO intervention Wednesday, so this is positioning rather than official action.

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: Aussie-yen, 112.23, down 1.31% from 113.73, overnight range 112.13 to 113.91. Read against AUD/USD, which is UP 0.34% overnight - so this is not Australian weakness, it is yen strength, and the same holds for the euro cross. Dollar-yen is down 1.76% at 155.87 from 158.66, a one-month high for the yen, having traded above 160 as recently as Tuesday. Applying the funding-squeeze test explicitly: the crosses are down 1.3% to 1.8%, which does clear the 1.5% threshold on dollar-yen, but the second and third conditions FAIL - VXN is 21.07 and FALLING against the 28 to 30 that a genuine carry unwind requires, equity futures are flat, and the dollar is broadly SOFT rather than firm. Verdict: a yen-specific policy repricing, NOT a funding squeeze. It is the instrument to watch, because a real unwind would appear here first.
